question: True or false: a pupil moved to a school of stronger classmates tends to rate their own ability higher?
answer: False. Marsh and Hau, using data from 26 countries, found the big-fish-little-pond effect: pupils of the same ability rate themselves lower in schools where classmates are stronger. Self-image is set by the people nearby, not by any absolute scale. The same pupil feels clever in one school and slow in another.
move: Your sense of your own ability is borrowed from the people around you.
ask: Whom do I measure myself against every day, and is that the fairest group to pick?
trap: Better company seems to lift how capable a pupil feels.
reference: Marsh and Hau, Big-fish-little-pond effect on academic self-concept: A cross-cultural (26-country) test of the negative effects of academically selective schools, American Psychologist, 2003
